title: Crate Stacker
tags: tens and ones,place value,two-digit numbers,greater than,less than,equal,compare numbers,add within 100,ten more,ten less,count to 120,first grade,grade 1,math,maths,3d,trucks,crates,toy town,read aloud,learning
description: Load toy trucks in a busy 3D loading yard! Stack towers of ten crates and loose crates to build numbers, see which truck has more and pick the sign, then add more crates up to 100. Every instruction is read aloud, so new readers can play too.
notes: Number Quest Launchpad Unit 3, The Tens Trellis (grade 1): a Kit 2 game on Oomba3D 1.1.0 in the Toy Town theme 1.1.0 (daytime, ink outlines, gear button, graphics 'auto'), loaded with exactly kit2ImportMap() (tests/unit/crate-stacker.test.js checks the literal map). The town behind the yard is the theme's own pieces (buildings, road, cars that drive by, trees, street lights), with a soft haze in front of it so the crates stand out; the crates, towers, trucks, cart and number boards are the game's own simple meshes (the theme's hatchback pulls the cart on wide screens). One loose orange crate is a ONE; a blue tower of ten crates is a TEN. Made for a child who is only starting to read: every instruction is short, shown and spoken through BRB.speak (voice role friendly; the speaker button says it again), numbers are big, and everything is done with big buttons or by tapping a truck. No timer, no lives, no fail state: a wrong answer wobbles the button and the truck (a dashed outline on the button with reduced motion) and gets a spoken hint, then another try. Three chapters of six rounds, made by window.CrateStacker.round(chapter, n, lap) (the block between /* crate-stacker:begin */ and /* crate-stacker:end */, pure, seeded from the round number; a replay lap gets new numbers): build (step 3.1; 1.NBT.B.2, also 1.NBT.A.1): rounds 1-3 load a number with 'Add a ten', 'Add a one', 'Take one off' and 'Go' (a teen, a number to 49, then a number to 99 asked as '5 tens and 3 ones' with the numeral hidden until Go); the chip shows '3 tens and 5 ones' live, and a tenth loose crate snaps the ten into a tower ('10 ones make 1 ten'); rounds 4-6 read a load and pick its number from three (the digits swapped, 34 or 43; no loose crates, 40 not 4; ten towers and a few crates, 101-109). greater (3.2; 1.NBT.B.3): rounds 1-3 'Which truck has more?' (different tens; the same tens; numerals only with the digits swapped), answered on a number button or by tapping the truck; rounds 4-6 pick the sign >, = or < for the two numbers (one round each, in an order made from the lap: different tens where the smaller number has the bigger ones digit, the same number twice, the same tens; round 6 numerals only), said as 'is greater than', 'is equal to', 'is less than' with the reason ('5 tens is more than 3 tens'). add (3.3; 1.NBT.C.4, 1.NBT.C.5): 1 a number and 20-40 more (towers hop on, the sign counts up by tens), 2 ten more, 3 ones more inside the ten, 4 ones more that fill a tower first (15 and 5 make 20, 3 more makes 23), 5 ten less (a tower rides away on the cart), 6 round 4 with bigger numbers; three number buttons, the wrong ones a real mistake (the tens added as ones, the new ten forgotten). Totals stay under 100. The player picks one of the theme's five adventurers as a helper; in a round the helper rides on the cab roof. Lesson mode: BRB.params { chapter: build | greater | add, lock: 1 } opens that chapter only; finishing its six rounds calls BRB.gameOver({ won: true }) once (the single call site), which completes the course step. With no parameters a picture menu offers the three chapters. Save: BRB.storage 'crate-stacker-v1' holds only which chapters are finished. Layout: wide screens set two trucks side by side, tall phones put the first on a loading dock behind the second; the camera backs off until the play area fits between the words and the buttons. Keyboard: every answer is a button (Tab, Enter, Space). A device without WebGL2 or import maps gets the site's 'needs a newer device' card. Words: English only (the I18N block, read by server/services/tts-lines.js for AI voices). Test handle: window.__cs (also window.__brbTest): state(), fast(), hero(id), act('ten' | 'one' | 'off' | 'go'), act('answer', v), spot('a' | 'b'), heroAt().
